title: 美国高校被逼：动用压箱底钱，200校已破例
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: Amanda, there's been a lot of talk lately that a lot of small colleges are coming up against a wall.
segments.zh: 阿曼达，最近很多讨论说不少小型高校正面临困境。

segments.en: Yes, we reported that colleges are turning to their endowment funds, which is kind of this sacred pot of money. And they're doing this in the hopes of
segments.zh: 是的，我们报道过高校动用捐赠基金，这笔钱通常被视为神圣储备。他们这么做是希望

segments.en: extending their chance of survival, kind of providing a buffer when enrollment is dropping.
segments.zh: 在招生下降时提供缓冲，以延长生存机会。

segments.en: So we have seen actually 200 schools that have reportedly drawn into restricted endowment money, which is a very problematic step for colleges. And so we reported on a school called Hiram
segments.zh: 实际上，我们看到约200所学校动用了受限捐赠资金，这对高校来说是非常棘手的一步。我们报道了俄亥俄州的希拉姆学院

segments.en: in Ohio that has done this. And even its auditors have warned that this is actually creating like severe financial risks or a going concern of warning for this school. So this is really
segments.zh: 该校就这么做了。连审计师都警告，这正造成严重的财务风险，甚至对该校的持续经营能力提出质疑。这确实

segments.en: emblematic of the pressures that small private colleges are under right now. They're facing rising expenses, enrollment pressures. So it's really kind of a perfect storm of factors that
segments.zh: 体现了小型私立高校当前面临的压力。他们面临开支上升、招生压力，可以说是多种因素叠加的完美风暴。

segments.en: colleges are facing right now. Well, obviously it's very risky and you don't know if you'll ever be able to fill those endowments up again. So what is the strategy? Is it just sort of a spend and hope
segments.zh: 显然这非常冒险，你不知道能否再填补这些捐赠基金。那么策略是什么？现在只是花钱然后祈祷吗？

segments.en: at this point? So schools just to generalize a little bit. They plan to in many cases repay these, they're calling them loans. They plan to repay the money. And so they use it on specific strategies.
segments.zh: 简单概括一下，许多学校计划偿还这些所谓的贷款，他们打算还钱，并将资金用于特定策略。
